summary: Two independently sourced identities from Thailand and Mexico. No human efficacy extrapolated from cellular antiviral assays or nutritional composition.
research_method: Primary Thai cell-based study; Mexican food-composition and public biocultural research; chemistry cross-referenced to IMPPAT and PubChem.

Panduratin A verified structure and chemical identifiers
sources.organization: IMPPAT, Institute of Mathematical Sciences, India

sources.organization: Universidad de Guadalajara and Mexican research institutions

organisms.geographic_context: Thailand and mainland Southeast Asia; culinary and regional herbal traditions
organisms.part_and_preparation_note: Rhizome; food preparations differ chemically from laboratory solvent extracts and isolated panduratin A

organisms.geographic_context: Mexico, especially maize-growing regions; public food traditions
organisms.part_and_preparation_note: Immature maize galls used as food; stage, maize cultivar and cooking alter composition

occurrences.note: Cyclohexenyl chalcone derivative; purified panduratin A inhibited SARS-CoV-2 infection in Vero E6 cells (post-entry IC50 0.81 µM), not clinical evidence; specific direct viral target unproven.
Fungal sterol measured in huitlacoche; not evidence of a therapeutic effect.
Phenolic abundance varies with maize genotype and developmental stage; not a single chemical entity.

domain_notes.text: No established human metabolic effect from fingerroot; experimental metabolic signaling reports are not clinical evidence.
Thai study: purified panduratin A suppressed viral replication in Vero E6 and Calu-3 cell cultures; no human treatment efficacy established.
Contains macronutrients and sterols as food; no demonstrated specific human metabolic treatment outcome.
Mexican studies quantified phenolics, fatty acids and ergosterol; laboratory antioxidant assays do not prove disease prevention.
No demonstrated direct human cognitive effect.
No demonstrated direct human mood effect.

safety.alert: Culinary rhizome use is not equivalent to concentrated panduratin A; no validated human antiviral dose or treatment safety. Cell cytotoxicity measured in the Thai study.
Food use involves identified, appropriately handled edible galls; laboratory or agricultural smut cultures are not automatically food-safe. Composition depends on maize and harvest stage.

cultural_uses.tradition: Thai culinary and publicly documented herbal uses
cultural_uses.preparation: Culinary ingredient, distinct from purified chemical
cultural_uses.reported_use: Fingerroot is used as a regional culinary aromatic; pharmacological study discusses established culinary use.
cultural_uses.limitations: The paper documents broad culinary context, not a specific community practice or antiviral clinical benefit.

cultural_uses.reported_use: Traditionally valued as a food and condiment in Mexican gastronomy.
cultural_uses.limitations: Public culinary record only; no medicinal efficacy claim or restricted knowledge.

structures.scope: specific stereochemically defined small molecule; 2D via authoritative CID
structures.binding_warning: Structure and cell inhibition do not prove direct binding, human antiviral efficacy, or safe exposure.
